reflections.summary: Lost 0-2 in the series. Game 2 was lost due to a compounding chain of setbacks: Mimikyu's Play Rough missing Milotic on Turn 2 was the first critical swing, leaving the team without an early KO on the opponent's primary bulky pivot. The burn on Aegislash from Talonflame's Flare Blitz (Turn 4) gutted the King's Shield stall strategy that was the defensive backbone against Garchomp's Earthquake PP break. Aegislash lasted only one more turn after burning. Milotic proved to be the true linchpin of the opponent's team — its Toxic crippled every switch-in, Recover kept it healthy, and it survived the entire game to clean with a final Muddy Water. Mega Floette underperformed as a threat; it was Toxic'd early, took heavy Brave Bird chip from Skarmory, and contributed limited damage before fainting. Toxapex was the MVP with Recover and Toxic but eventually ran out of recovery against stacked chip. In the final turn, Garchomp's Earthquake broke through Toxapex and Mimikyu, and Milotic mopped up. No between-game adjustments meaningfully backfired, but the inability to punish Milotic or preserve Aegislash's longevity were the decisive failures.
reflections.adjustment: For a rematch: (1) Bring Swampert over one of the current six — it is immune to Earthquake and resists Water, making it the ideal Milotic and Garchomp answer while providing its own Ground STAB pressure. (2) Prepare a sun setter (Torkoal) to cripple Milotic's recovery and shift momentum; sun also powers up Meowscarada as a potential surprise offensive pivot. (3) Prioritize removing Milotic early and relentlessly — it is the opponent's true win condition enabler. (4) Avoid relying on Aegislash as the sole King's Shield staller against Garchomp without a burn-proof backup; consider holding a status absorber or pivoting faster. (5) Do not Mega Evolve Floette early if Toxic is on the field — Mega Floette's longevity is overstated and it becomes set-up fodder.
reflections.notebook: Opponent core identity: Garchomp (Life Orb, Jolly) is the primary win condition via Earthquake PP-breaking through King's Shield. Milotic (Leftovers, Bold) is the defensive backbone — Toxic cripples physical attackers, Recover sustains, Muddy Water is the main STAB, Haze resets setup. Floette-Eternal Mega (Fairy Aura, Timid) is a surprise Mega pick; Moonblast is dangerous but it is vulnerable to Toxic and physical pressure. Talonflame (Focus Sash, Jolly) provides speed control via Gale Wings Tailwind and Taunt support; Brave Bird is a nuke. Untapped reserves: Hatterene (Trick Room, Psychic, DazzlingGleam, Magic Bounce) and Scrafty (Intimidate, FakeOut, KnockOff) are surprise picks for game 3. Key tactical facts: Mimikyu's Disguise buys exactly one hit; opponent will Taunt to neutralize it. King's Shield PP can be broken with two Earthquakes in a row if they don't double. Milotic's Muddy Water accuracy is imperfect — it missed twice in this game. Toxic transfer chains are their midgame plan: they Toxic whatever switches in and stall with Milotic's recovery. Tailwind from Talonflame elevates their entire team's speed tier. Prep priority for next series: bring a Ground-immune or Water-resistant pivot (Swampert ideal), pack status removal or Toxic-proof options, and have a plan to break Milotic before it becomes unmanageable.

reflections.summary: Won game 2 and the series 2-0 through a well-suited four of Talonflame, Garchomp, Milotic, and Mega Floette. Talonflame's turn-1 Taunt denied Mimikyu's Swords Dance option, while Garchomp's Earthquake broke Disguise and created immediate spread pressure. Although Garchomp was left at 6%, Talonflame and Milotic established the tempo needed for Mega Floette's Energy Ball pressure on Toxapex and Talonflame's Flare Blitz damage on Aegislash. The decisive endgame was using Garchomp's final Earthquake to remove Mimikyu and leave Toxapex in Muddy Water range. Mega Floette was the appropriate evolution: Fairy Aura-boosted Fairy damage and Energy Ball gave the brought four both offensive coverage and a direct Toxapex answer. Milotic was valuable for sustained spread pressure, Tailwind support enabled the midgame, and the lead matched well into Mimikyu/Aegislash. The full registered six fit reasonably well, but the supplied evidence does not establish that an unused member offered a materially better game-2 alternative. There is no game-1 record or stated between-game change, so whether any explicit adjustment helped or backfired cannot be determined; game 2 itself was piloted without recorded decision errors. The 2-0 series result is authoritative.
reflections.adjustment: For a future series, retain the Talonflame/Garchomp/Milotic/Mega Floette core when expecting Mimikyu, Aegislash, and Toxapex. Continue using early Taunt and spread damage to constrain Mimikyu, but preserve Garchomp more carefully when possible because it is an excellent late-game Earthquake closer against the revealed structure. Against Toxapex, commit simultaneous pressure from Mega Floette's Energy Ball plus a second attack rather than relying on Milotic's Muddy Water alone, which allowed Recover opportunities and can miss. Plan for Toxic attrition on both bulky attackers and avoid treating a low-health Toxapex as secured until it is covered through Recover. No roster substitution is supported by the evidence alone; reconsider unused options only if future preview information shows a specific matchup need.
reflections.notebook: Opponent revealed Mimikyu with Focus Sash, Disguise, Play Rough, Shadow Claw, Shadow Ball, and Swords Dance; Taunt is highly useful before it can boost, and spread damage efficiently breaks Disguise and covers it late. Aegislash repeatedly used King's Shield and showed Shadow Sneak, Flash Cannon, Sacred Sword, and Leftovers; pressure it with Fire coverage and avoid giving it passive turns. Toxapex showed Regenerator, Shell Bell, Toxic, Recover, Haze, and Liquidation; it seeks Toxic-based attrition and can reset pressure with Recover, so use simultaneous strong attacks, especially Grass coverage, rather than Water-chip cycles. Skarmory showed Sturdy, Tailwind, Roost, Spikes, and Brave Bird; account for Tailwind and its ability to trade physical damage into Fairy attackers. Mega Floette's Energy Ball was the clearest Toxapex-breaking tool, while Milotic provided durable spread pressure but should not be the sole Toxapex answer. Talonflame's Taunt and Tailwind were strategically valuable despite its short lifespan.
